To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Status:** Privileged / for negotiation purposes. Seller material treated as adversarial draft.

## 1. Headline view

The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced" and says several matters are "addressed". Its own Disclosure Letter contradicts that: it concedes that the Bluefen consent is not obtained, the Riverlark debt is not repaid or released, the Ironquay IP has not transferred, the AUD 420k bonuses are missing from the funds flow, and the privacy incident is uninvestigated. Read together, the Seller is asking us to (a) accept a very thin liability regime, and (b) simultaneously give us "knowledge" of every known problem via the Disclosure Letter so that clause 8.3 and the general disclosure then strip warranty recourse for those very problems.

The structural trap is this: **warranties will not protect us on anything in paragraphs 2–10 of the Disclosure Letter.** Those known matters must be dealt with by conditions precedent, Completion deliverables, price/debt adjustments and specific indemnities sitting outside the general caps. The general warranty regime is then for the unknowns, and it needs to be materially stronger than proposed.

Quantified known exposures already identified: Riverlark ~3.2m, bonuses 0.42m plus on-costs (~0.5m), Ironquay 0.18m, Sandbar 0.33m, Bluefen revenue at risk 3.6m p.a., plus an unquantified privacy incident. That is roughly AUD 4.2m of hard items before the Bluefen and incident risk – against a proposed total cap of AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m deal.

## 2. Liability architecture (Clauses 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5)

**2.1 Cap – 20% / AUD 4.8m.** Low end of Australian mid-market and plainly inadequate given the identified issue profile. Push to 50% at minimum, or 100% if W&I insurance is not being used. If the Seller insists on 20%, the trade is: specific indemnities and fundamental/tax/IP warranties sit outside it, and the Seller funds a retention/escrow (suggest 10–15% for 18–24 months) so the cap is actually recoverable against a venture vehicle that may distribute proceeds.

**2.2 Thresholds.** De minimis of AUD 25k is high (~0.1% of price); propose AUD 10k. Basket of AUD 250k is acceptable in size (~1%) but it is drafted as a *deductible* (excess only). Push for a *tipping* basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded), which is the more common Australian position. Specific indemnities, tax, title/capacity and fraud must be excluded from both thresholds.

**2.3 Time limits.** 18 months does not allow one full audit cycle post-Completion; 24 months is the market floor for general warranties. Tax warranties/indemnity: 7 years (ATO amendment periods run 4 years standard, unlimited for fraud/evasion). Title/capacity: at least 6 years (contract limitation period in NSW), preferably unlimited or 12 years if executed as a deed.

**2.4 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" – reject outright.** This is a drafting device that drags indemnity claims, tax claims, completion accounts/leakage adjustments, breach of covenant and fraud under the cap, basket and 18-month cut-off. The default should be the reverse: limitations apply only to Warranty Claims, and only where expressly stated.

**2.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 applying to "all Claims of any nature".** Same problem in three places. Mandatory carve-outs from caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance: fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct, wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers; all specific indemnities; the tax indemnity; price adjustment / leakage; equitable relief (injunction/specific performance for restraints and confidentiality); and liability that cannot lawfully be excluded (note: a non-reliance clause will be given weight on s18 ACL claims but cannot exclude them outright – we should preserve that position rather than contractually concede it).

**2.6 Fundamental / title / capacity warranties "subject to the same caps and time limits for administrative simplicity" – reject.** There is no administrative burden in a second line of drafting. Title and capacity should be capped at 100% of the price and survive for the limitation period. A buyer that pays AUD 24m and discovers it does not own the shares cannot be limited to 4.8m for 18 months.

## 3. Disclosure and knowledge (Schedule 7, Disclosure Letter, Clause 8.3)

**3.1 General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers.** Reject. Insist on a "fair disclosure" standard: a matter is disclosed only if fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely consequences. Public registers (ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia, court lists) should not be deemed disclosed at all – we commissioned our own searches for our own purposes, not to indemnify the Seller's warranties. If we must accept data room disclosure, it should be limited to documents in the agreed index as at a fixed date, delivered on a USB/agreed archive, and still subject to the fair disclosure test.

**3.2 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge, including advisers and anything "discoverable".** This is the most damaging single provision in the package. Constructive knowledge ("discoverable from the data room or public records") plus imputed adviser knowledge means almost any warranty breach can be defended on the basis that we *could* have found it. Reject. If a knowledge qualifier survives at all, limit it to the *actual* knowledge, at signing, of two or three named Wattlebridge individuals, excluding adviser knowledge, excluding anything "discoverable", and expressly not applying to specific indemnities or to matters the Seller was obliged to disclose and failed to. Better: delete and rely on the fair disclosure regime.

**3.3 Disclosure Letter mechanics.** Data room cut-off is 22 September 2026; today is 4 November. Require an updated Disclosure Letter at signing and a bring-down at Completion. Any new disclosure between signing and Completion must not qualify the Completion warranties (notification only), and material new matters should give us a termination right or price adjustment. Paragraph 1.4 (no admission of anything) is standard, but should be matched by a Buyer reservation that acceptance of the letter does not constitute acknowledgment that any matter is fairly disclosed.

## 4. Known issues – each needs a specific mechanism

**4.1 Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of revenue; change-of-control clause 11.2, conditions 11.3).** The cover note says "addressed"; the Disclosure Letter says no consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are met. Required position:
- Buyer-only waivable condition precedent: written consent from Bluefen, unconditional or with all 11.3 conditions satisfied, in form reasonably acceptable to us, and not on amended commercial terms (no price concessions, new termination rights or scope reductions).
- "Reasonable endeavours" is too soft and "treat as satisfied on delivery of written consent" is not acceptable if the consent is conditional. Require all reasonable endeavours, Buyer participation in discussions, and copies of all correspondence.
- End Date with termination right; consider a Bluefen-specific price retention or deferred consideration released if Bluefen does not terminate/materially reduce within 12 months post-Completion.

**4.2 Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m; change-of-control 8.1, discharge 9.2).** A post-Completion release is incompatible with a debt-free/cash-free deal and with clause 8.1 (a share transfer without consent is likely an event of default on day one). Required position: payout letter agreed pre-Completion; repayment at Completion out of the purchase price via the funds flow (Buyer pays Riverlark directly); executed deed of release and PPSR discharge (and release of any Seller or Company guarantees) delivered at Completion. Check whether Riverlark holds security over the *shares* – this also goes to title (see 4.9).

**4.3 Ironquay (SOW3; AUD 180k open; IP transfers only on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees).** The Seller's indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" misdescribes the risk: the exposure is not AUD 180k, it is that the Company does not own project materials that may sit inside its product. Required position:
- Payment of all SOW3 fees pre-Completion (or treat as Debt in the price), with Ironquay's receipt and a confirmatory IP assignment as Completion deliverables.
- Specific indemnity for all loss arising from any failure of IP in any Ironquay SOW to vest in the Company, outside caps/basket.
- Diligence follow-up: confirm no equivalent conditions in SOW1/2 or other developer contracts, and that employee/contractor IP assignments are in place.

**4.4 Completion bonuses (AUD 420k, DD-005).** "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism. The payer is the Company, post-Completion, with superannuation (~12%) and NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) on top – realistically ~AUD 495k+. Required position: treated as Transaction Costs / Debt-like items deducted from the price, grossed up for on-costs, itemised in the funds flow; or Seller funds the Company to pay them pre-Completion. Also confirm the continued-employment conditions do not create retention cliff risk for key staff we are relying on.

**4.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records).** "Not expected to be material" rests on a preliminary investigation that has not determined access, scope or notification. Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach scheme, the Company has 30 days from awareness to assess whether a reasonable person would conclude serious harm is likely; penalties are now substantial and a statutory privacy tort exists. Customer contracts (likely Bluefen) probably contain their own incident notification obligations. Required position:
- Pre-signing: completed investigation, access logs, legal assessment of notification obligations, and confirmation of whether customer notification clauses are triggered.
- Specific indemnity for all costs and losses (investigation, OAIC/regulatory, notification, remediation, customer claims, contractual penalties), outside caps/basket, with Buyer control of conduct post-Completion.
- Warranty of no other incidents and of compliance with privacy and data security obligations, not qualified by this disclosure.

**4.6 Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k; DD-008 and DD-011 "read together").** The Seller's own instruction to read them together suggests one commitment split into three. Questions to put: were these committed before the accounts/locked-box date; are they for past or future service; are they terminable; are they related-party; were they in the FY26 budget/working capital normalisation; and why are they documented across two data room items. If they are liabilities incurred pre-Completion for past service, they are Debt-like and come off the price. "Ordinary course" is an assertion, not a disclosure.

**4.7 Office lease (DD-007).** Confirm whether the notification is pre- or post-transfer, whether failure gives the landlord a termination right, and make the notice a Completion deliverable (Seller to give it in agreed form).

**4.8 Mossvale (DD-009).** The Seller is probably right that a share sale is not an "assignment", but we need to read the actual clause for deemed-assignment or change-of-control language. Take a clean warranty that no third-party consent is required for the transaction under any Material Contract, and a specific indemnity if Mossvale asserts otherwise.

**4.9 Title.** The share register is the Company's own record and is not conclusive. Our verification should include: ASIC current extract and historical share transfer filings; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (share security to Riverlark?); constitution (pre-emptive rights, transfer approval, drag/tag); share certificates or statutory declaration of loss; confirmation of no options, convertibles, SAFEs or employee equity; Seller board/shareholder approvals and capacity. Title warranty uncapped and unqualified by disclosure.

**4.10 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime".** Not acceptable for an analytics business. Tax: standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, 7-year survival, cap at 100% of price, no knowledge or disclosure qualification. IP: own/valid licence of all IP used in the products, no infringement claims, open-source compliance, source code control, employee/contractor assignments – with a higher cap (we propose 100%) and 3-year survival given the Ironquay gap.

## 5. Price mechanics

"Debt-free/cash-free" needs definitions that actually capture what we have found. Debt / Debt-like items must expressly include: Riverlark principal, interest and break costs; unpaid Ironquay fees; Completion bonuses plus on-costs; any Sandbar amounts incurred pre-Completion; accrued but unpaid tax; and costs of the DD-006 incident to the extent incurred or reasonably estimable. Confirm whether this is completion accounts or locked box; if locked box, leakage definitions must catch the bonuses and any Seller-directed payments, with leakage uncapped and outside thresholds.

## 6. Summary of recommended positions

| Area | Seller proposal | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% (4.8m) | 50% minimum; 100% absent W&I; escrow/retention 10–15% |
| De minimis / basket | 25k / 250k deductible | 10k / 250k tipping |
| General warranty period | 18 months | 24 months |
| Tax | General regime | Separate indemnity, 7 years, 100% cap |
| Title / capacity | Same as general | 100% cap, limitation period or unlimited |
| IP | General regime | 100% cap, 3 years; Ironquay indemnity |
| "All limitations apply to all Claims" | Default-in | Reverse: only Warranty Claims, only where stated |
| Carve-outs | None | Fraud, wilful misconduct, indemnities, tax, leakage, equitable relief |
| Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | Fair disclosure standard; no public registers; updated letter and bring-down |
| Clause 8.3 knowledge | Constructive, advisers, "discoverable" | Delete; fallback actual knowledge of named individuals, no indemnity impact |
| Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent | Buyer-waivable CP; unconditional consent; End Date; retention |
| Riverlark | Release post-Completion | Payout and release/PPSR discharge at Completion via funds flow |
| Ironquay | Indemnity limited to 180k payment | Pay pre-Completion; confirmatory assignment at Completion; IP indemnity uncapped |
| Bonuses | Not in funds flow | Debt-like, grossed up for super/payroll tax, itemised |
| Privacy incident | "Not material" | Complete investigation pre-signing; specific indemnity; Buyer conduct |
| Sandbar | Ordinary course | Information request; Debt-like if pre-Completion liability |
| Mossvale / lease | Not needed / notification only | Clause review; warranty + indemnity; notice as Completion deliverable |
| Title | Share register | Independent verification (ASIC, PPSR, constitution); uncapped warranty |

## 7. Immediate next steps

1. Send a consolidated information request on Sandbar, Ironquay SOWs 1–2, DD-006 investigation status and access logs, Riverlark security package and payout figure, and Bluefen correspondence to date.
2. Run ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia and court searches against the Company and Seller ourselves.
3. Decide the W&I insurance question now – it determines how hard we push on cap and escrow.
4. Respond to the Seller with a mark-up that moves all known issues into CPs, deliverables, price adjustments and specific indemnities, and resets the general regime per the table above. Lead with the point that the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts the cover note's characterisation of matters as "addressed".

I can turn any of these into draft clause language for the mark-up if useful.
